content: If July is the stock market’s critical test, then so far, so good. Upbeat earnings, lower jobless claims, inflation still under 3% and newly passed tax cuts have all combined to keep the market grinding higher. But is this as good as it gets?

title: Kganyago Sees South Africa CPI Staying in Target Despite Risks
content: South Africa’s central bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago signaled confidence that inflation would remain within its target for the next two years, despite uncertainties stemming from US tariffs.

title: Milei Tightens Grip on Argentina Currency Market Left Awash in Pesos
content: Investors in Argentina began to anticipate a subtle policy change as President Javier Milei seemed to ease his control of how many pesos circulate in the economy, a trade-off between inflation and economic growth ahead of October midterm elections.

title: Carney Should Bar US Firms From Projects as Trade Leverage, Scotiabank’s Holt Says
content: Canada should consider excluding US companies from major infrastructure and defense projects as part of its response to the Trump administration’s barrage of tariffs, according to a Bank of Nova Scotia economist.

title: Trump Likely to Fire Powell Soon, White House Official Says
content: President Donald Trump is likely to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell soon, a White House official said, and discussed the possible move in a meeting with congressional Republicans on Tuesday night.

title: French Government Risks Ire With Further Cut to Savings Rate
content: The French government said it will cut the rate on regulated savings products used by millions of households, a day after unveiling plans to slash spending and scrap two national holidays to help repair public finances.

title: ECB Should Cut Rates to Weaken Euro, Italy’s Deputy Premier Says
content: The European Central Bank should reduce borrowing costs to help the economy by weakening the single currency, Italian Deputy Premier Antonio Tajani said.

title: Hassett Grabs Pole Position in Race to Be Trump’s New Fed Chair
content: Kevin Hassett, one of President Donald Trump’s longest-serving economic aides, is the early frontrunner to replace Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve chief next year, according to people familiar with the process.

title: Pound Risks Worst Run in a Decade Ahead of Key Labor Market Data
content: The pound headed for its longest slide in a decade as traders looked ahead to key labor market data that could bolster the case for interest-rate cuts.

title: Trump Softens Tone on China to Secure Xi Summit and a Trade Deal
content: President Donald Trump has dialed down his confrontational tone with China in an effort to secure a summit with counterpart Xi Jinping and a trade deal with the world’s second-largest economy, people familiar with internal deliberations said.

title: Swiss Trade Deal With US Is Awaiting Trump’s Sign Off, Bern Says
content: Swiss officials approved the draft of a framework trade deal with the US almost two weeks ago, and are continuing talks while awaiting sign off from President Donald Trump, according to the government.

title: Fed’s Barr Warns of Booms and Busts Tied to Weakened Bank Rules
content: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr emphasized that regulation must evolve with the financial system, issuing a warning as Trump-era officials look to ease rules for big banks and shift to a lighter touch.

title: Why UK Inflation Is So High and What It Means for Interest Rates
content: While a post-pandemic burst of inflation has abated across much of the developed world, Britain is still stuck with the highest price growth among big western economies.

title: Spain Housing Supply Plunges 20% During Quarter as Prices Soar
content: The number of homes for sale on Spain’s main real estate listings website fell by 20% in the second quarter, the biggest drop since at least 2007 and a sign of the challenge the country faces to address its housing crunch.

title: US Industrial Production Rises on Pickup in Utility Output
content: US industrial production rose in June for the first time in four months, boosted by a jump in utility output and a modest gain in manufacturing.

title: US Producer Prices Stagnated on Decline in Services Costs
content: US wholesale inflation moderated in June as a sharp decline in the costs of travel-related services blunted a pickup in goods prices.

title: Barclays Sees Senegal’s Debt Burden Easing After Data is Rebased
content: Senegal’s heavy debt burden, which has triggered its second credit-rating downgrade in five months, could ease sharply when the government does a technical reset of economic data later this year, according to Barclays Plc.

title: Thailand to Make Fresh Proposals to US in Bid to Avert Tariff
content: Thailand’s finance minister will present fresh proposals to US trade officials in talks scheduled for Wednesday, the latest effort by the nation to avoid a 36% tariff threatened by President Donald Trump.

title: Portugal Is Set to Replace Centeno as Central Bank Governor
content: Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro plans to replace central bank Governor Mario Centeno after his first term ends July 19, according to a person familiar with the premier’s thinking.

title: Indonesia Sees ‘New Era’ of Trade With US Under Trump Deal
content: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Wednesday confirmed he struck a 19% tariff deal with US President Donald Trump.

title: Southeast Asia’s Biggest Economy Becomes a Global Dealmaker
content: I’m Chris Anstey, an economics editor in Boston. Today we’re looking at international deal-making by Southeast Asia’s biggest economy. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so  here.

title: US Home Purchase Applications Fall After Prior Week’s Surge
content: US mortgage applications to buy a home declined last week to the lowest level since late May as borrowing costs remained elevated.

title: Trump Says Coca-Cola Agrees to Use Cane Sugar for Coke
content: President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post that Coca-Cola Co. has agreed to use cane sugar in Coke beverages sold in the US.

title: Walmart Eliminates Hundreds of Store-Support, Training Jobs
content: Walmart Inc. is cutting hundreds of store-support roles, its latest move to simplify structure at the world’s largest retailer.

title: Sarepta Soars as Gene Therapy Stays on Market With Warning
content: Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. shares soared after the company said it was cutting more than a third of its workforce and that its gene therapy for a fatal muscle disorder would stay on the market with warnings about the potential for liver failure.

title: Hong Kong’s $25 Billion Debt Woe Sparks Talks on ‘Bad Bank’
content: The pile of soured debt at Hong Kong lenders has grown so large that some in the industry have discussed the creation of a “bad bank” to soak up the financial hub’s non-performing loans.

title: Singapore Luxury Condo’s Early Flop Shows Property Boom’s Limits
content: A large-scale luxury development in Singapore sold only a tiny fraction of units when it started accepting bookings, reflecting the struggles of the priciest segment in the city-state’s otherwise stratospheric property market.

title: BAE Sees ‘Phenomenal Pace’ on Next Fighter Jet as Rival Sputters
content: BAE Systems Plc said it is speeding ahead with the development of its next-generation Tempest fighter jet, as a rival European program is hamstrung by Franco-German squabbling.

title: BAE Says Drone-Fired Rocket Shows Path to Cheap Air Defense
content: BAE Systems Plc said a drone shot down an uncrewed aircraft using a laser-guided rocket, in what the UK defense company called a “major step forward” in the quest for low-cost air defense.

title: Tesla Readies a Six-Seat Version of the Model Y for China
content: Tesla Inc. is preparing to launch a longer, six-seat version of its Model Y sport utility vehicle in China, where the carmaker has been losing ground to domestic manufacturers with fresher lineups.

title: United Refines Profit Target on Rebounding Travel Demand
content: United Airlines Holdings Inc. refined its profit outlook for this year as travel rebounds, adding a dose of optimism following a bleak few months punctuated by flight disruptions, trade tensions and fighting in the Middle East.

title: Construction Costs to ‘Go Up Radically,’ Prologis CEO Says
content: The chief executive officer of Prologis Inc., a real estate investment trust that owns and runs warehouses, said US immigration policy is causing a labor shortage that’s driving building costs higher.

title: Starwood Strikes $2.2 Billion Real Estate Deal With Brookfield
content: Starwood Property Trust agreed to acquire Fundamental Income Properties for $2.2 billion as Chief Executive Officer Barry Sternlicht aims to further diversify the company’s revenue.

title: Tesla Failed to Stop Autopilot Misuse, Safety Expert Testifies
content: Tesla Inc. hasn’t done enough to protect against drivers misusing its Autopilot system, a safety expert testified at a trial over a 2019 fatal collision.

title: JPMorgan Kicks Off US Bank Borrowing With $4 Billion Sale
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. tapped the US investment-grade bond market Wednesday, kicking off what’s expected to be a relatively light season for bank bond sales ahead of expected changes to sector regulations.

title: Morgan Stanley Beats Rivals With Heftiest Equity Underwriting Haul Since 2021
content: Whiplashing trade war updates held up some capital raising at the beginning of the second quarter, but a June comeback led to Morgan Stanley’s best global equity underwriting fee haul since the fourth quarter of 2021.

title: Trump’s Auto Safety Pick Promises Rapid Self-Driving Deployment
content: President Donald Trump’s choice to lead the nation’s top car safety regulator pledged to prioritize safety while at the same time making it easier for automakers to deploy-self driving cars.

title: Wall Street Traders Supercharged by Tariffs That Stymied Deals
content: Wall Street banks were optimistic Donald Trump’s second term would unleash a dealmaking boom. Instead, it’s delivered a trading bonanza.

title: Montreal Airport Plans $7.3 Billion Revamp With Government Backing
content: Montreal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport will spend as much as C$10 billion ($7.3 billion) over the next decade to modernize and expand its facilities.

title: PNC Considers Charging Fintechs for Access to Customer Data
content: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. is considering charging financial-technology companies for access to valuable customer data, following the lead of JPMorgan Chase & Co., Chief Executive Officer Bill Demchak said.

title: Diageo Turns to CFO to Begin Turnaround After Crew’s Sudden Exit
content: Diageo Plc is replacing Chief Executive Officer Debra Crew after a miserable two years that have undermined the distiller’s strategy of trying to get consumers to trade up to more expensive drinks.

title: KKR Mulls Acquisition of Health-Care Technology Firm GPI
content: KKR & Co., the buyout firm that’s been scouting for takeover targets amid the recent market volatility, is considering a potential acquisition of Italian health-care technology firm GPI SpA, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: JPMorgan Is Now Worth More Than Three Largest Rivals Combined
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. keeps putting more distance between itself and key rivals.

title: Oil Prices in Mid-$60s Is Profit Red Zone, Quantum Capital Says
content: Activity is slowing in US oil fields as drillers remain in the crude-price danger zone for profits, according to one of the biggest investors of private operators in the shale patch.

title: Wall Street’s Prime Brokerage Boom Lures European Rivals
content: The industry’s revenue from prime brokerage is expected to hit a record $30.8 billion this year and European banks are hustling to get a bigger piece of that action.

title: ASML Cools 2026 Growth Outlook as Clients Balk at Trade Wars
content: ASML Holding NV Chief Executive Officer Christophe Fouquet walked back his forecast that sales will grow next year, blaming trade disputes and global tensions.

title: Citigroup Poaches Two Senior JPMorgan Bankers in Hiring Push
content: Citigroup Inc. is hiring two of JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s senior bankers, as the US lender continues to tap its Wall Street rival for talent to bolster its own investment banking division.

title: Severe Obesity in US Children Has More Than Tripled Since 2008
content: The proportion of severely overweight children in the US has skyrocketed in recent years, with the highest rates seen in adolescents and Black children, a new study found.

title: Morgan Stanley CEO Sees Banks Clawing Back Private Credit Gains
content: Morgan Stanley Chief Executive Officer Ted Pick said “the tide may begin to shift” in the ocean of private credit.

title: Biggest Banks’ Loan Yields Keep Falling Even as Fed Remains Wary
content: President Donald Trump is frustrated that the Federal Reserve hasn’t lowered interest rates this year. At the biggest US banks, loan yields are steadily dropping anyway.

title: Goldman Plans Deals to Put Private Investments in 401(k) Funds
content: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is in talks to put its private-market investments into US retirement funds, a step to bringing the Wall Street firm’s products to more mainstream investors as rules ease.
